title: JSX Basics
description: Learn JSX syntax, expressions, and how it differs from HTML.

data.text: **JSX** (JavaScript XML) is a syntax extension for JavaScript that lets you write HTML-like code inside your JavaScript files. It's the foundation of React development and makes building UIs intuitive and readable.
JSX stands for JavaScript XML. It allows you to write HTML elements in JavaScript and place them in the DOM without using functions like `createElement()` or `appendChild()`.

data.title: JSX vs createElement
data.content: Comparing JSX with traditional DOM creation

data.text: You can embed any JavaScript expression inside JSX by wrapping it in curly braces `{}`. This includes variables, function calls, and calculations.

data.title: JSX Style Example

data.text: JSX Must Have One Root Element
JSX expressions must have a single parent element. You can use a `<div>` or a React Fragment (`<>...</>`) to wrap multiple elements.

data.title: Wrapping Elements
data.content: Using Fragments to avoid extra DOM nodes

data.title: Common Mistake
data.text: Returning multiple elements without a wrapper will cause an error. Always wrap sibling elements in a single parent or Fragment.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: JSX is HTML-like syntax that compiles to JavaScript
Use curly braces {} to embed JavaScript expressions
JSX uses camelCase for attributes (className, onClick)
All tags must be closed in JSX
Return a single root element or use Fragment
data.takeaway: With JSX knowledge, you're ready to create your first React application!
